items.text: Once the BSc is finished, the question stops being "which degree" and becomes "what now.".

items.heading: An Msc in Biotechnology
items.text: An MSc in Biotechnology is not one generic next step.

items.heading: A Bsc Biotechnology Student
items.text: A BSc biotechnology student can also look at MSc microbiology, agricultural biotechnology, biology or statistics, depending on interest and eligibility. Microbiology leads to labs, pharma and food quality, and statistics leads toward data and research roles.

items.heading: Shortlist the Msc Specialisation
items.text: Shortlist the MSc specialisation or the job-first lane you are genuinely leaning toward. Do not weigh all six specialisations and every entry-level role at once. Pick the one MSc specialisation and the one job-first lane that fit your actual interest and constraints.

items.heading: Run the Four Questions
items.text: Run the four questions on both options. Check fit, money and time context, real market evidence, and how each path holds up against AI and automation pressure.

items.heading: Complete One Proof Task
items.text: Complete one proof task for your top option. Attempt a real JAM or GAT-B mock paper, document a lab project, or apply to one real lab-technician or QC opening, something that tests genuine interest, not imagined interest.

items.heading: Verify Current Eligibility and Cutoffs
items.text: Verify current eligibility and cutoffs on the official exam or recruiter pages. Confirm this year's JAM, CUET-PG, or GAT-B eligibility, or the specific employer's qualification requirement, directly on the official source before committing time or money.
